comment: Declared differences between BC's own metadata emitter and the runner's
SymbolReference-derived MetaTable. Issue #3533.
This file IS the allowlist: MetadataEquivalenceHarnessTests fails on any difference not
listed here, and equally on any entry here that no longer matches anything. So a reader
fix must delete its entries in the same change, and a BC version that introduces a new
property surfaces as a new undeclared difference rather than passing silently.
Every entry carries a reason AND exactly one KIND of reason, because the four kinds need
different evidence:
issue            a defect, tracked, expected to go away
outOfScope       the runner does not implement the surface, so no AL test can see it
(needs a Doc pointer)
oracleLimitation the ground truth is the wrong shape for this member, so the difference
says nothing about the runner (needs a Doc pointer)
cannotExpress    the symbol file cannot express it AND it cannot be derived
NO ENTRY CURRENTLY CLAIMS cannotExpress. Seven TranslationKey entries did, on the evidence
that SymbolReference.json stores no translation keys. That was true and the conclusion was
wrong twice over: the key is COMPUTED from names rather than stored (2,153 of 2,153
reproduced), and the runner reads no translation files anyway, so it is out of scope rather
than impossible. 'Nothing is stored' is evidence about storage, never about derivability.
Nine entries are DIRECTION-SCOPED. An entry covers both directions unless it says otherwise,
and a reason that justifies one direction must not license the other. All three
oracleLimitation entries are runner-only: they exist because the runner shows a merged
runtime view, so BC-absent / runner-present is what they justify — while the reverse, BC
emitting a field the runner never builds, is a hard reader defect that must still fail.
There is deliberately NO occurrence cap. One was implemented and used by nothing, which made
the PR claim a ratchet the code did not keep. No entry here has a bound that survives a
rebuild — the counts move with the BC build and with which apps are bundled — so any cap
would be a number nobody measured. Direction narrows categorically instead.
Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over Business Foundation (12 tables) and System Application
(138 tables): 67,344 differences across 65 members. #3568 removed six of them -- 688
differences on MetaKey.KeyName / Clustered / Unique / SumIndexFields, MetaKey.DebuggerDisplay
and FieldMetadataRelation.Name -- see docs/metadata-equivalence.md#keys. Per-member counts
and examples are on issue #3568.
PageDefinition was added to the comparison by #3782 step 1, and the 117 entries below are the
result. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 over Business Foundation and System Application (235
pages): 32,958 differences across 124 members.
READ THE 117 CAREFULLY: 49 of them are #field / *Specified COMPANION entries, which BC's own
serializer sets from the same value as the member declared beside them. So there are 68 DISTINCT
members, not 117, and comparing the raw count against the table side's overstates the page gap.
issue 3784  55 entries (30 distinct members). Properties SymbolReference.json already carries
and EmitPageXml does not read -- including the Actions (106 pages), Methods (107)
and Views (4) arrays. Extensible is the sharpest: the runner hardcodes "1", BC
answers 0 on 104 of 235 pages, and the symbol file states Extensible=0 for ALL 104
with zero omissions, so it is a pure read-don't-guess fix.
outOfScope  62 entries (38 distinct members). The ordinary field-control tree the runner does
not build today, plus the translation keys.
NONE of the outOfScope page entries claims a value is UNDERIVABLE, and that distinction is the
point. An earlier draft of this file said the control tree could not be proven faithful because
the symbol file stores AL text rather than the compiled DataColumnName. That was wrong, and it
would have recorded a live architecture question as settled: DataColumnName IS the field number,
control ids are identical in both sources, and 442 of 442 Rec-bound controls resolve exactly
against this harness's ground truth. ControlGUID is likewise a pure encoding of (page id,
control id) -- 5,001 of 5,001 exact. Both are cost/scope decisions with a proof path, which is
what these entries now say.
MEASURED ON ONE BC BUILD, EVALUATED ON THREE (eight on main). A difference exists only if the
object carrying it exists on that version AND declares the property shape that produces it, and
BC moves both between minors -- so an entry can be correct on two legs and match nothing on a
third, which the stale-entry check reports as a landed fix. That fired on 27.5 for four
InfopartPageDefinition entries: the only page with a part-control ProviderID is 4306 'Agent
Tasks' on 27.5 and 8705 'Table Information Card' on 28.x, and 27.5's part declares Editable
while 28.x's does not. Deleting them would have broken 27.0 and 28.4, where the differences are
real.
'versionContingent': true exempts an entry from the UNUSED check and from nothing else -- it is
still matched, so it can never hide a difference. 15 of the 117 page entries carry it: every one
whose whole population on the measured build is one or two occurrences, not just the four that
27.5 happened to hit. See docs/metadata-equivalence.md#one-build-measured-three-evaluated.
Measurement caveat: ONE BC build and TWO apps. Base Application's ~4,000 pages are not measured
at all -- apps.json excludes it because its emit needs a .NET reference no BC artifact ships
(#3549) -- so nothing here is evidence about the pages most AL tests actually touch.
The seven pre-existing TranslationKey.* entries already covered the page side without being
touched: they match on member signature, and pages carry the same TranslationKey type.

differences.reason: The field-name or property-name component of a translation-file lookup id. SCOPE DECISION BY THE REPOSITORY OWNER, 2026-09-10 (relayed on #3568): translations are out of scope for the runner. In the owner's terms, translations are not relevant right now and nothing in a run has ever had to do with them. So this is a surface the runner does not need to reproduce -- decided, not assumed, and not a statement that the derivation is correct. WHAT THE RUNNER ANSWERS HERE IS UNMEASURED, NOT RIGHT: 0 and Module are what the MetaField ctor's own defaults leave behind, on a surface nothing exercises. Nobody has checked them against BC and nobody should spend effort doing so. Corroborating the decision rather than grounding it: the runner has no .xlf or Translations/ handling anywhere -- zero references in AlRunner/ -- and docs/limitations.md records that it installs no BC translation resources, so no AL test could observe this member today even if the scope call went the other way. Separately measured, and the reason this can never be called a permanent LIMIT: the key IS derivable -- (uint)(FNV-1a-32 over the UTF-16LE bytes of the name + int.MaxValue) reproduces 2,153 of 2,153 keys in the ground truth (TranslationKeysAreDerivable_NotAPermanentLimit). Deriving it is possible and simply not wanted. What invalidates this entry is the owner putting translations back in scope. NOT to be confused with MetaField.CaptionML, which is the caption TEXT, is AL-observable, and is declared separately as a defect.

BC states the field's real CLR type and the runner states the empty string on all 1,888 fields. ClrType is not an XML attribute at all — BC derives it itself — and it is a PURE FUNCTION of Datatype, which the symbol file does carry and the runner already reads: measured over 988 observations, all 16 Datatypes map to exactly one ClrType each (BigInteger->System.Int64, GUID->System.Guid, Code/Text/DateFormula->System.String, Option/Integer->System.Int32, BLOB/RecordID->System.Byte[], Media->NSMediaWrapper, and so on). Recoverable with no app data.

BC states the object's AL namespace on every field; the runner states the empty string. The symbol file has no ALNamespace attribute, but its Namespaces nesting is exactly what the attribute names.

BC builds a MultiLanguage caption for the field; the runner builds none. The symbol file carries Caption (2,743 occurrences in System Application) — the MultiLanguage object is its runtime form. Direction-scoped to BC-present / runner-absent; the runner inventing a caption BC does not have is a different defect.
BC answers Undefined where nothing is declared; the runner answers None, a different member of the same enum. An encoded-default disagreement, not a missing read.
BC answers true on a field with no declared TestTableRelation; the runner answers false. AL's real default, not the constructor's.

BC answers AsReadOnly where the runner answers ToBeClassified. The symbol file states AllowInCustomizations only where it is non-default, so this is the AL default being wrong rather than a value being lost.

BC gives SystemCreatedBy and SystemModifiedBy a TableRelation to User (2000000120); the runner gives them none. This is the difference already observable from plain AL as FieldRef.Relation() answering 0 — see #3549. Direction-scoped to BC-present / runner-absent; the runner inventing a relation BC does not have would be a different defect and is not covered.
BC answers false on the platform-added system fields; the runner answers true. Restricted to the fields BC adds, not to declared ones.
Same gap as MetaField.ALNamespace, on keys, where the runner answers null.

BC derives this as the POSITIONAL FIELD SPEC over field ids ("Field1,Field2"), not as a name anyone declared, and NCLMetaKey.CreateFromMetaKey never passes it — the declared AL name travels as MetaKey.KeyName, which the reader now states (#3568). So no AL surface can observe this member, and the runner keeps its own spelling rather than reproducing a spec BC regenerates. Superseded reason, recorded because it hid a real defect: this used to read "two different naming schemes", and MetaKey.KeyName was declared as "the same disagreement on the second of the two name properties". That was wrong — KeyName is the DECLARED name, the symbol file states it verbatim, and it reaches AL through ObsolescenceGuard.ThrowIfObsoleted.
The same null-versus-empty-string shape as the MetaField entries, running the other way: BC states the empty string and the runner states null.
BC names the platform-added system fields $systemId, $systemCreatedAt and so on; the runner uses the AL spelling (SystemId). BC policy for the fields IT adds, which the runner adds itself.
Same gap as MetaField.ALNamespace, on the table itself.
BC marks every table as having had its platform fields added; the runner leaves the flag false even though it adds those fields.
BC answers Personalization where the runner answers Cloud. The symbol file carries Scope.
BC answers true where the runner answers false, on fields whose AL declares an OnValidate trigger.
BC states the declared inherent entitlements; the runner answers None. The symbol file carries InherentEntitlements (687 occurrences in System Application).
The permissions half of MetaTable.InherentEntitlements, same shape and same source.

The private backing storage behind MetaTable.FieldsById, holding the same merged tableextension fields as MetaTable.Fields.<presence>; same runtime-merged-versus-build-time-emit boundary, same consequence for an empty diff.

The runner models the MERGED RUNTIME state a running system has — every registered app's tableextension fields present on the base table. The ground truth is BC's BUILD-TIME per-app emit, which by construction sees only the app being compiled. Two different things, so this is a limitation of the oracle and not evidence about the runner: 115 fields on four Business Foundation tables (230, 242, 308, 6635). In BC 29 everything is merged at database level anyway, which makes the runner's merged view the forward-looking one. CONSEQUENCE: a multi-app bundle can never produce an empty diff, so a non-empty diff here is expected and must not be read as noise or as a bug. DIRECTION-SCOPED: covers only BC-absent / runner-present, which is the merged-runtime direction this reason justifies. The reverse — BC emitted a field and the runner built none — is a hard reader defect and is NOT covered.
The by-id index of the same merged tableextension fields as MetaTable.Fields.<presence>; same runtime-merged-versus-build-time-emit boundary, same consequence for an empty diff.
BC answers true unless AL declares otherwise; the runner answers false. The symbol file states ReplicateData only when non-default.
BC states Internal on fields whose AL declares it; the runner answers Public. The symbol file carries Access.
Same as MetaField.Access, on the table.
A case disagreement: BC answers Lookup, the runner answers LOOKUP. The runner is echoing the AL source text rather than mapping it to BC's enum spelling.

The reverse direction: BC's table Caption is null and the runner carries a real caption. The runner resolves it from AL and BC leaves the runtime object's Caption unset, answering through CaptionML instead. Direction-scoped to BC-null / runner-present, which is the direction this reason describes; BC stating a caption the runner drops is not covered.

The page's control tree, which the runner does not reconstruct TODAY. A cost and scope decision, not a limit of the symbol file, and deliberately not a claim that the values cannot be obtained: SymbolReference.json carries the control tree with its SourceExpression as AL text (Rec."No."), while BC's document carries the compiled DataColumnName -- which IS the field number, resolvable through table metadata the runner already builds. Measured with this harness's own ground truth on BC 28.1.49838.53910: every Rec-bound control whose source table is in the bundle resolves exactly, 442 of 442 with zero wrong numbers, the residuals being two understood normalisation categories (field names differing in case or spacing, and controls bound to a page VARIABLE, which BC names "Control" + the id of the first control bound to that variable). Control ids are identical in both sources, so each derived value is independently checkable against the ground truth. The resolution machinery already exists and is in use -- EmitSubFormLinkXml resolves SubFormLink field names to numeric ids off the part's and the host's SourceTable. What is missing is the work, tracked on #2460 for actions; this entry records that it has not been done, never that it could not be.

A deterministic ENCODING of the page id and the control id, not an opaque designer token. Verified exactly on this harness's own ground truth: 5,001 of 5,001 control GUIDs across both apps on BC 28.1.49838.53910 (and 5,035 of 5,035 on 28.4.53241.54407) are reproduced character-for-character by   {<pageId:08x>-<ctlId & 0xFFFF:04x>-0000-0c<(ctlId >> 24) & 0xFF:02x>-<(ctlId >> 16) & 0xFF:02x>00836bd2d2} -- e.g. page 257 control 791368264 gives {00000101-5248-0000-0c2f-2b00836bd2d2}. Both inputs are in SymbolReference.json, so this is computable rather than unavailable. It is declared here because the runner emits no control tree for these ids to belong to (see the Controls entries), and it becomes a gap to close the moment it does -- NOT because the value cannot be derived.
